data.title: Beta-carotene
data.summary: Photoprotective agents · Carotenoid (provitamin A); systemic photoprotective
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Photoprotective agents_

**Class:** Carotenoid (provitamin A); systemic photoprotective

## Mechanism of action
- Quenches singlet oxygen and free radicals generated by light-activated porphyrins
- Deposits in skin → carotenodermia (yellow-orange colour)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Erythropoietic protoporphyria (classic indication; modest benefit — afamelanotide is newer)
- Polymorphous light eruption, solar urticaria, hydroa vacciniforme (limited evidence)

## Dose & formulations
- Adults 60–180 mg/day (children 30–90 mg/day), aiming for blood carotene of 600–800 µg/dL; protection begins after 1–2 months

## Adverse effects
- Carotenodermia (palms, soles, nasolabial — sclera spared, unlike jaundice)
- Loose stools; increased lung cancer risk in smokers and asbestos workers at high doses

## Contraindications
- Smokers (lung cancer risk)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Considered safe.

## Viva points
- Carotenaemia spares the sclera
- Used in erythropoietic protoporphyria
- Avoid in smokers

_Sources: Khopkar (Systemic photoprotective agents); Wolverton 4e ch.40. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
